name: Urgent Care / Outpatient Clinic
description: Fast-paced walk-in clinic treating non-emergent acute conditions. Smaller than a hospital with streamlined operations focused on rapid patient turnover, extended hours, and convenient access. Typical for single-site or multi-site urgent care chains.

org_structure.overview: The urgent care clinic is organized for speed and efficiency. A clinic manager or owner oversees business operations while a medical director provides clinical leadership. Providers (MDs, DOs, NPs, PAs) handle patient visits with support from medical assistants, front desk staff, and limited on-site lab and X-ray. Billing and insurance verification are handled by front office staff or a centralized billing team in multi-site organizations. The model emphasizes minimal hierarchy and rapid decision-making.

departments.name: Leadership & Management
departments.description: Clinic ownership/management and clinical leadership. Sets hours, staffing levels, payer contracts, and clinical protocols.

roles.title: Clinic Manager / Owner
roles.description: Business operations: staffing, scheduling, P&L, supply ordering, facility management, payer contracting.

roles.title: Medical Director
roles.description: Clinical oversight: protocols, peer review, provider credentialing, quality assurance. May also see patients.

departments.name: Clinical Providers
departments.description: Clinicians delivering direct patient care. Mix of physicians and advanced practice providers for maximum flexibility and cost efficiency.

roles.title: Physician (MD/DO) — Urgent Care
roles.description: Diagnoses and treats acute conditions (infections, minor injuries, lacerations, fractures). Performs procedures such as suturing, splinting, I&D.

roles.title: Nurse Practitioner (NP)
roles.description: Independent or collaborative practice managing patient visits, prescribing medications, ordering and interpreting tests.

roles.title: Physician Assistant (PA)
roles.description: Medical evaluation and treatment under physician supervision or collaborative agreement; suturing, casting, wound care.

departments.name: Nursing & Clinical Support
departments.description: Clinical support staff assisting providers with patient care, procedures, and room turnover.

roles.title: Registered Nurse (RN) / Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN)
roles.description: Patient triage, intake, vital signs, medication administration, wound care, IV starts, assisting with procedures.

roles.title: Medical Assistant (MA)
roles.description: Rooming patients, vitals, EKGs, immunization administration, lab specimen collection, front-back support.

departments.name: Radiology & Lab
departments.description: Point-of-care lab testing and limited X-ray services. Often cross-trained staff or outsourced to reference labs.

roles.title: X-Ray Technician / Radiologic Technologist
roles.description: Performs and processes X-rays (chest, extremity); may be cross-trained as MA. Reports to Medical Director for protocol.

roles.title: Lab Technician
roles.description: Performs CLIA-waived point-of-care tests: strep, flu, UTI, pregnancy, glucose, mono, COVID-19. May be delegated to MAs.

departments.name: Front Office & Billing
departments.description: Patient check-in, scheduling, phone management, insurance verification, and payment collection. Often the first and last impression.

roles.title: Front Desk / Patient Services Representative
roles.description: Patient check-in/out, insurance verification, copay collection, appointment scheduling, phone and message management.

roles.title: Medical Biller / Coder
roles.description: Coding (CPT/ICD-10), claims submission, payment posting, denial management, patient statements. May be centralized in multi-site ops.

roles.title: Referral Coordinator
roles.description: Arranges specialist referrals, radiology referrals, and follow-up appointments for patients needing higher-level care.

key_relationships: Medical Director and Clinic Manager share joint responsibility for clinic performance — clinical quality alongside financial and operational results.
Providers and Medical Assistants work in paired teams for efficient room turnover and patient throughput (often 3-4 patients per hour per provider).
Front desk coordinates closely with clinical staff to manage wait times and communicate delays to patients.
Clinic Manager oversees supply ordering and facility maintenance; providers communicate supply and equipment needs through the manager.
X-Ray Tech and Lab staff support all providers equally, with protocols set by the Medical Director.
Billing team coordinates with front desk for accurate insurance capture at check-in to minimize claim denials.
